content:
natalie: FYI — multiple inference pods pending in us-west-2a, GPU nodepool shows 0 allocatable IPs and CA isn't bringing up new nodes for that AZ. High customer impact on realtime endpoints.

ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-nodepool-usw2a - PodsPending=42 CPUPressure=NoSchedule - triggered at 2026-03-18T14:20:34Z :rotating_light:

cheng: I'm looking. Initial hypothesis: ENI/IP exhaustion in the AZ causing kubelet to fail attach and scheduler to avoid the nodegroup. Also seeing lots of spot preemptions earlier which may have fragmented capacity.

ryan: Can you paste `kubectl get pods` for the pending ones? any nodeSelector/affinity forcing AZ?

cheng: paste below (trimmed):
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending
inference-job-abcde   0/1   Pending   0   3m  <none>   us-west-2a   <none>
inference-job-fghij   0/1   Pending   0   4m  <none>   us-west-2a   <none>
```

cheng: And CA logs showing refusal: 
```
I0318 14:18:21.123 autoscaler.go:312] ScaleUp: no scale-up: max nodes in group gpu-nodepool-usw2a reached or blocked by cloud provider
I0318 14:18:22.456 cloudprovider/aws/aws_cloud.go:789] CreateInstanceGroup: ENI quota exceeded in subnet subnet-xxxx
```

natalie: Ok so it's not purely scheduler logic — AWS subnet/ENI limits per AZ are the choke. We just hit a burst of cron-driven load that spawned many parallel large-batch jobs. Those were using a legacy nodeSelector for `zone: us-west-2a` which amplified pressure.

ryan: Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) pause the cron that fans out jobs to 2) taint the gpu nodepool to prevent new scheduling 3) spin up a new nodepool in us-west-2b with identical labels and drain some queued pods into it via temporary patching. Who can do the taint now?

oncall-sre: I can. Doing quick steps: cordon + taint on gpu-nodepool-usw2a managed nodes: `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-nodepool-usw2a` then `kubectl cordon` and `kubectl taint nodes key=gpu-burst:NoSchedule` to stop new pods.

oncall-sre: Done. Taint applied to 12 nodes.

cheng: Paused the cron that fans out the batch jobs (kube cron controller updated). Also added a temporary admission webhook rule to reject pods with hard AZ nodeSelector for us-west-2a.

ryan: Spun up a new nodepool gpu-fallback-usw2b (on-demand mixed G5s) with nodePool.maxSize=40, labels match inference route. CA picked them up and started scheduling.

ops-bot: [INFO] nodepool gpu-fallback-usw2b created by ryan - 12 instances provisioning.

cheng: We're seeing the backlog drain now. 28 pods moved to new nodes in usw2b, latency returning to normal.

natalie: Great. For follow-ups: escalate to infra to request larger ENI/ip-per-subnet quota or move pods to use IPv6 ENI mode. Also need to clean up the legacy AZ pinning in the job template and add per-job concurrency controls.

ryan: Filed INFRA-1242 for ENI quota increase + CIDR plan. Also opened SRE-749 to remove hard zone selectors and add workload-level backpressure.

cheng: Quick config changes we made to avoid repeat: set cluster-autoscaler flags `--max-node-provision-time=10m --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m` (temporary), add `priorityClass=system-cluster-critical` to realtime endpoints, and a `preemptionPolicy=Never` for batch jobs to reduce thrash.

natalie: Note on cost: switched fallback pool to on-demand which will increase spend for the incident window. Finance informed.

ops-bot: [RESOLVED] gpu-nodepool-exhaustion - routing restored, backlog cleared. Incident status: mitigated.

ryan: Postmortem items: 1) Remove AZ pinning from templates 2) Add per-workload concurrency caps 3) ENI/subnet quota request and better monitoring (alert on ENI utilization per subnet) 4) autoscaler policy review 5) bake a fallback nodepool in each region that avoids spot churn.

natalie: Thanks all — closing thread. Please add timeline + logs to SRE-749. :thumbsup:
